spans.text: 5. Why a pull Queue + 2-hour Cron matters
attach the canonical event queue to a normal push consumer if the objective is to let ClickHouse sleep.

A push consumer automatically consumes continuously. Delaying each message by two hours only creates a two-hour-offset continuous stream; after the initial delay it can still keep ClickHouse awake around the clock.

blocks.text:
00:00 - 01:59   Queue accumulates
02:00           flush wakes ClickHouse
02:00-02:0x     drain queue + insert
02:0x           snapshot/materialized work complete
02:0x+idle      ClickHouse scales down

02:00 - 03:59   Queue accumulates
04:00           next flush
...

spans.text: Cloudflare Cron Trigger on a dedicated flush Worker;
cron expression conceptually every two hours;
scheduled Worker repeatedly pulls batches until:
execution time budget is nearly exhausted;

Cloudflare documents pull consumers specifically for cases where upstream consumption needs to be rate/availability controlled. Pull batch size currently supports up to 100 messages. Queue retention on Paid can be configured up to 14 days, giving ample recovery room for a 2-hour cadence.
Cloudflare Cron Triggers run in UTC.
Do not encode business meaning into the exact UTC boundary. “Every two hours” is an operational flush interval, not a reporting-day definition.
